Jawara is a dance form preformed by the peasants of Madhya Pradesh. Jawara is performed in the Bundelkhand area of Madhya Pradesh. The folk-dance form, Jawara, is basically a peasant dance, which is performed by the peasants of the Bundelkhand region upon the reaping of the harvest, in celebration of prosperity. Both men and women wear colourful costumes to participate in this dance. Women also carry baskets full of jowar (broom-corn) on their heads while dancing.

The State Bank of India is popularly known as SBI was formed when the Bank of Madras merged into two other presidency banks - the Bank of Calcutta and the Bank of Bombay in January 1921, to form the Imperial Bank of India.

The imperial bank of India was later renamed as the State Bank of India on July 1, 1955.

The State Bank of India is not included under the list of nationalized banks as it was already a state-owned financial institution in the country at the time of its inception.

A basic law regarding flow of currents was discovered by G.S. Ohm who was on born March 16, 1789 in Erlangen, Bavaria Germany.

In 1828, long before the physical mechanism responsible for flow of currents was discovered. Imagine a conductor through which a current I is flowing and let V be the potential difference between the ends of the conductor.

Then Ohm's law states that V ∝ I or, V = R I (3.3) where the constant of proportionality R is called the resistance of the conductor.

The SI units of resistance is ohm, and is denoted by the symbol Ω.

questions.question: Jellyfish are an example of which type of phylum? जेलिफ़िश किस संघ से संबंधित है?
questions.solution:
Jelly Fish belong to the kingdom Animalia and phylum Cnidaria.

The phylum Cnidaria includes soft-bodied stinging animals such as corals, sea anemones, and jellyfish.

This phylum consists of radially or radially symmetrical aquatic invertebrates having unique stinging structures in the tentacles surrounding the mouth.

Flag Satyagrahas were conducted most notably in the city of Jabalpur and Nagpur in 1923 but also in many other parts of India.

The news of flag hoisting in Jabalpur spread like fire in the country and after flags were hoisted at several places across the country.

The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, formerly known as Victoria Terminus Station, in Mumbai, is an outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India, blended with themes deriving from Indian traditional architecture.

The building, designed by the British architect F. W. Stevens, became the symbol of Bombay as the 'Gothic City' and the major international mercantile port of India.

The terminal was built over 10 years, starting in 1878, according to a High Victorian Gothic design based on late medieval Italian models. Its remarkable stone dome, turrets, pointed arches and eccentric ground plan are close to traditional Indian palace architecture.

Chikan embroidery is produced in the city of Lucknow, the capital of the state of Uttar Pradesh, India. Although the geographical origins of Chikan embroidery are uncertain, most written accounts trace it back to East Bengal.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. His elder sister taught him English.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

His elder sister taught him English.

options.text: His elder sister is taught English by him.
options.html: His elder sister is taught English by him.

options.text: He has been taught English by his elder sister.
options.html: He has been taught English by his elder sister.

options.text: He was taught English by his elder sister.
options.html: He was taught English by his elder sister.

options.text: He is being taught English by his elder sister.
options.html: He is being taught English by his elder sister.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form ("was" in this sentence) of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Real Madrid won the Champions League. (Active Voice)

The Champions League was won by Real Madrid. (Passive Voice)

The options except (c) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c): He was taught English by his elder sister.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. No effort has been made by the Indian cricket team to cash off on its vibrant image in the World Cup.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

No effort has been made by the Indian cricket team to cash off on its vibrant image in the World Cup.
questions.solution:
The only meaningful phrasal verbs with the word 'cash' are 'to cash in' and 'to cash up'.

So, options c) and d) are incorrect.

When cashiers and storekeepers cash up, they add up all the money taken from customers during a shift, or at the end of the working day. This phrasal verb does not fit in the given sentence which discusses that the cricket team had made no efforts towards a certain thing in World Cup.

'To cash in on' means 'to get money or another advantage from an event or situation, often in an unfair way'.

The phrase gives the meaning that the Indian cricket team did not unfairly use its vibrant image to get any advantage in the World Cup. It forms a meaningful sentence.

Hence, option a) is correct.

Note: Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Those who follow a healthy routine is likely enjoying good health.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Those who follow a healthy routine is likely enjoying good health.
questions.solution:
Since the subject is plural in nature, the verb agreeing to it should also be plural. This means that the singular verb 'is' incorrect and it should be replaced with 'are' [plural verb].

So, the segment in option a) has an error.

Hence, option a) is correct.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The mathematical calculation of this problem is easy than a previous one.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

The mathematical calculation of this problem is easy than a previous one.
questions.solution:
Only two things are being compared in this sentence, i.e., the mathematical calculations of two problems.

The comparative degree of an adjective is required when the two things are compared. Since 'easy' is an adjective ofa positive degree, an improvement is required in underlined phrase.

Replacing 'easy' with 'easier' (comparative degree) rectifies this error.

Also, since two particular problems are being compared, the definite article 'the' should be used before 'previous one' (signifying the 'problem' dealt with previously).

The correct sentence is: The mathematical calculation of this problem is easier than the previous one.

Hence, option a) is correct.

Note: · The Positive Degree of an Adjective is the Adjective in its simple form. It is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree of an adjective denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.solution:
Has/have/had (when used as auxiliary verb) should be followed by the past participle form of verb (i.e., V3), whereas 'began' is the past simple form of verb (i.e., V2).

It should be replaced with 'begun' to rectify the error.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. The teacher said to me, "You have not submitted the assignment."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

The teacher said to me, "You have not submitted the assignment."

options.text: The teacher said me that I had not submitted the assignment.
options.html: The teacher said me that I had not submitted the assignment.

options.text: The teacher told me that I had not submitted the assignment.
options.html: The teacher told me that I had not submitted the assignment.

options.text: The teacher said to me that I have not submitted the assignment.
options.html: The teacher said to me that I have not submitted the assignment.

options.text: The teacher told to me that I have not submitted that assignment.
options.html: The teacher told to me that I have not submitted that assignment.

questions.solution:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Present Perfect Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Tense.

Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object) should be converted into Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

I. Reporting verb 'said to' will change to 'told'.

II. The pronoun 'you' will change to 'I'.

III. 'Have not' will change to 'had not'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): The teacher told me that I had not submitted the assignment.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. This is because of its aroma, flavour and variety in the market. B. Thus, it leads to poor health and mental disorders among children. C. Children as well as teenagers are tempted towards junk food. D. It has no or negligible nutritional value and high content of sugar and salt.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. This is because of its aroma, flavour and variety in the market.

B. Thus, it leads to poor health and mental disorders among children.

C. Children as well as teenagers are tempted towards junk food.

D. It has no or negligible nutritional value and high content of sugar and salt.
questions.solution:
Sentence (A) cannot start the passage as it is not clear what 'this' refers to. Similarly, sentence (B) cannot start the passage as we don't know what 'it' refers to.

Sentence (C) is an apt introductory sentence which starts a discussion on children's urge to have junk food.

Sentence (A) gives reason behind this urge. So, 'this' in sentence (A) refers to the urge of children to eat junk food, mentioned in (C).

DB is a necessary pair. Sentence (D) explains how such food has no nutritional value, and sentence (B) explains the negative effect because of negligible nutritional value.

So, the correct order is: CADB.

Hence, option d) is correct.

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. They can then purchase them on subsidized rates with additional loan facilities. B. It will import technologically advanced medical instruments and provide them to entrepreneurs. C. The Indian Government has announced certain facilities in the budget session. D. This will help in strengthening the economic condition of entrepreneurs.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. They can then purchase them on subsidized rates with additional loan facilities.

B. It will import technologically advanced medical instruments and provide them to entrepreneurs.

C. The Indian Government has announced certain facilities in the budget session.

D. This will help in strengthening the economic condition of entrepreneurs.
questions.solution:
Sentences (B) and (D) do not start the passage as it is not clear what 'it' in (B) and 'this' in (D) refer to.

Sentence (C) starts the passage and informs what the Indian Government announced in the budget session.

'It' in sentence (B) refers to 'the Indian Government'. Sentence (B) follows (C) and mentions the announcement by the Government that it will import medical instruments and provide them to entrepreneurs.

The pair A-D mentions how this will help the entrepreneurs. 'They' in (A) refers to entrepreneurs mentioned in (B). (D) concludes the passage and informs about the overall effect of this decision on the entrepreneurs.

So, the correct order is: CBAD.

Hence, option d) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A reward is a ______ which motivates a person to achieve excellence in his field.

Both 'monument' and 'memorial' are built to remind people of a famous person or event. They can be named after/dedicated to a certain personality, but 'reward' is not associated with monuments/memorials.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank number (1).
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option for blank number (1).
questions.solution:
The blank should be filled with an adverb which aptly modifies the verb 'misunderstood' and fits the context of the passage.

'Happily' and 'proudly' are the adverbs which signify that the person is aware of his doings and intend to do things in a way (for example: She proudly sat in the first row to see her daughter get an award. OR She happily said yes to the job offer from her dream company).

Misunderstanding something is not an intentional act, so 'happily' and 'proudly' do not fit in the sentence. 'Slowly misunderstood' is not a meaningful phrase.

'Usually misunderstood' implies that people often think discipline to be a restriction.

So, filling the blank with 'usually' makes the sentence meaningful.

Hence, option d) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank number (2).
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option for blank number (2).
questions.solution:
The previous sentence discusses how 'discipline' is generally misunderstood to be a restriction to freedom. So, the word 'dream' cannot fit in the second blank to talk about discipline.

But the passage is overall in a positive tone with respect to 'discipline'. So, 'disadvantage' and 'curse' are not the correct words to describeit.

'Virtue' means 'behaviour which shows high moral standards'.

The word is fit to describe discipline and filling the second blank with 'virtue' gives the meaning that discipline is a behaviour with high moral standards and both students and professionals should practise it.

Hence, option a) is correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option for blank number (3).
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option for blank number (3).
questions.solution:
The third blank should be filled with a verb as there is no other verb in the sentence. And in English language, a sentence mandatorily needs to have a subject and a 'verb'.

Also, a verb is required to describe what happens to a disciplined person in each and every field of life.

So, options a) [adjective] and d) [noun] are incorrect.

Option b) is incorrect as it is a plural verb and the subject 'a disciplined person' is singular. So, it violates subject-verb agreement.

So, 'succeeds' [a singular verb] is fit for the blank.

Hence, option c) is correct.

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

Note: Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement.
